title: What we do not know
description: A standing register of the holes in this library, ranked by how much they block a decision. Compiled by walking the gaps arrays of every dataset and adding the questions nobody has asked yet.

blocking.question: What does maritime security actually cost today?
blocking.why_it_blocks: Every pricing argument we have rests on a 2012 figure. We cannot price a product against a fourteen-year-old anchor.
blocking.what_we_have: $5,000 per day for a four-man team, up to $60,000 per Gulf of Aden voyage, 2012, Cato.
blocking.how_to_close: A broker quote, or one conversation with a P&I club or a security provider. This is a phone call, not a research task.

blocking.question: What does it cost to run a ship for one day?
blocking.why_it_blocks: Without daily OPEX and charter rates we cannot express escort cost as a percentage of voyage cost, which is how a shipowner will judge it.
blocking.how_to_close: Moore OpCost report, or Clarksons. Both paid.

blocking.question: What did the Convoy Escort Programme actually charge, and what happened to it?
blocking.why_it_blocks: It is the only escort business model precedent we have, and our per-vessel figure is our own arithmetic on 2012 numbers.
blocking.what_we_have: About $30,000 for one boat escorting roughly four vessels for three to four days.
blocking.how_to_close: Companies House filings, trade press archive, or the people involved.

blocking.question: Has any commercial operator ever bought autonomous escort?
blocking.why_it_blocks: A deliberate search found zero. If the answer is genuinely never, the sales cycle is category creation, not displacement.
blocking.what_we_have: Nothing found. Nine of ten incumbents publish no client at all, so absence of evidence is weak evidence.
blocking.how_to_close: Ask a broker or a P&I club directly. They see the contracts.

blocking.question: How long is a ship actually exposed in the Bab el-Mandeb and southern Red Sea?
blocking.why_it_blocks: We have the Gulf of Aden corridor at 490 nm and 33-49 hours. The Houthi attacks happen further north and we have no equivalent figure.
blocking.how_to_close: Chart measurement plus a published transit corridor definition. Doable from open sources.

important.question: Is the 7.5-10% Hormuz war risk figure real?
important.note: Flagged as probably wrong. Reuters has Hormuz at 0.5%. It is currently displayed as a headline number in the app.

important.question: How many bulk carriers, tankers and container ships exist, by count not tonnage?
important.note: UNCTAD publishes the type split by DWT only. We cannot size the addressable fleet by hull.
important.how_to_close: Clarksons, Equasis annual report, or IHS.

important.question: Who are the charterers, and do they ever buy protection directly?
important.note: They bear the war risk premium on most charter types. We name one company, Cargill.
important.how_to_close: Research task. Trade press, fixture reports.

important.question: Who are the offshore energy operators, and do they buy differently?
important.note: Six of ten incumbents serve offshore. We have catalogued zero companies.

important.question: Who is the Company Security Officer at each target?
important.note: ISPS makes the role mandatory, so every company has one, but eight of sixteen publish no names. Searching by role rather than by company page should find them.

important.question: How many ships transited Suez in 2025 and 2026?
important.note: We have 2023 and 2024. The recovery or non-recovery is the demand signal for the whole product.

unasked.question: What is the legal position on an uncrewed vessel escorting a crewed one? Who is the master? Which COLREGs apply? Does a flag state have to approve it?
unasked.why: This may be the real constraint rather than the technology or the price. Nothing in this library touches it.

unasked.question: Would a P&I club or war risk underwriter reduce a premium for a vessel under escort, and by how much?
unasked.why: If yes, the product sells itself on the insurance line. If no, it is a pure cost and much harder.

unasked.question: What does BMP, the industry's own best management practice guidance, say about escort? Is it recognised at all?
unasked.why: If escort is not in BMP, a manager has no framework to justify buying it.

unasked.question: Who actually decides at a shipowner: the DPA, the CSO, the fleet director or the charterer? We have inferred it from the ISM and ISPS codes but never confirmed it with a practitioner.
unasked.why: The entire target list is built on this assumption.

unasked.question: What happened to the Convoy Escort Programme, and why did it stop?
unasked.why: The only precedent. Its failure mode is the thing most likely to repeat.

unasked.question: How does a shipowner currently procure armed guards? Through the manager, the charterer, a broker, or direct?
unasked.why: The purchase path for the substitute is the purchase path for us.

unasked.question: What is the actual attack probability per transit, and does any owner compute it?
unasked.why: 38 incidents against tens of thousands of transits is a very low per-voyage probability. If owners price it that way, the product is a hard sell regardless of premium.

data_sources_we_do_not_have.gives: Fleet counts by type, charter rates, newbuild and secondhand values, trade flows. The industry standard.
Daily operating cost benchmark by vessel type and size.
BDI, TCE assessments, tanker and dry bulk indices.
Vessel movements, ownership resolution, casualty data.
Registered owner, ISM manager, class and P&I per IMO number. Free but account required.
Ship particulars, company particulars, piracy reports.
Live vessel positions and transit counts through any corridor. Would let us compute exposure and traffic ourselves.
Container rate indices and contract rates.

note: Ranked by whether the answer changes a decision, not by how hard it is to get.
